Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3195); Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine:--Ituræa.
BiblicalUsage: Iturea is the region Philip the tetrarch ruled when John began to preach. In Luke 3:1, in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar, Philip is tetrarch of Iturea and of the region of Trachonitis, and John the son of Zacharias comes preaching in the wilderness.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Luke names the rulers to pin the gospel to real time: while Philip ruled Iturea, the word of God came to John.
RelatedPeople: John the Baptist; Philip the Tetrarch
